item.title: Photos: Best images from Hornets' 107-105 loss to Chicago
item.description: The Charlotte Hornets fell to the Chicago Bulls Wednesday night 107-105, going 0-4 in NBA Cup Group Play in Eastern Conference Group C with a point-differential of -71. It was another frustrating defeat for the Hornets, who've now lost six in a row. Once again, Charlotte was shorthanded, missing Kon Knueppel, Grayson Allen, Dennis Schroder and Ryan Kalkbrenner. That was no excuse, however, as Chicago played without Jalen Smith, Norman Powell and Caleb Wilson. Brandon Miller finished as the game's highest scorer, tallying 35 points, three rebounds, one assist and three steals. Naz Reid added 18 points and eight rebounds, while Christian Anderson Jr. had another solid showing, tallying 15 points on 5-for-9 shooting off the bench. For the Bulls, it was Matas Buzelis who dropped 24 on 8-for-15 shooting with five rebounds. Josh Giddey nearly posted another triple-double, finishing with 12 points, 11 rebounds and seven assists. item.title: 'A level below!' - PSG warned their squad players cannot replace injured stars Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Paris Saint-Germain face a major attacking dilemma after losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the rest of the season. Following a frustrating 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma, former stars Daniel Xuereb and Emmanuel Petit have raised serious doubts over the squad's depth ahead of the January transfer window. PSG's attacking crisis exposed against Roma PSG's offensive struggles were laid bare on Wednesday night as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Roma in the Champions League. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue both ruled out for the remainder of the campaign, the club's supporting cast failed to step up when needed most. Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts all endured disappointing outings against the Italian side. Their underwhelming displays immediately prompted concern from former PSG striker Xuereb and ex-Chelsea midfielder Petit, who both questioned whether the current squad can cope without their injured talismans. Xuereb questions quality of PSG's deputies Xuereb, a 1984 Olympic champion, offered a blunt assessment of the players tasked with filling the void. Speaking to Le Parisien , he argued that the replacements simply do not match the match-winning quality that has defined PSG's recent success. "Those who played on Wednesday lacked penetration, one-on-one duels and runs in behind," Xuereb said. "They are excellent players, internationals. But if they don't usually play, there are good reasons for that. When Doue and Kvaratskhelia are there, they are second-string players. They are a level below. "If PSG have achieved what they have over the past two or three seasons, it is thanks to players capable of scoring at any moment. Unfortunately, they are injured." Petit urges January action over cruciate fears Petit shares those concerns and believes PSG must enter the winter transfer market to find an attacking reinforcement. Speaking as a pundit on RMC , he stressed that recovering from cruciate ligament injuries is notoriously difficult, meaning the club must plan beyond the current campaign. "They have to explore every opportunity," Petit said. "When you tear your cruciate ligaments, those are not simple injuries. Rare are the players who have returned to their previous level. So the thinking for next summer can already happen in January. You are only looking at this season, whereas I am looking ahead to next season." Crucial winter transfer window awaits PSG PSG now face a defining period as the January transfer window approaches. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue sidelined for the rest of the season, the club's hierarchy must weigh up whether to pursue an immediate attacking signing or trust the options already at their disposal. If no suitable targets are available mid-season, the pressure will remain firmly on the likes of Akliouche, Torres and Godts to rediscover their sharpness.

item.title: Ohio State vs Michigan: Five reasons the Buckeyes win Saturday
item.description: Ohio State is 7-4. Michigan is 6-5. Neither team is playing for anything but pride on Saturday. They say this is a rivalry game where you throw the records out, and for once both teams might actually like to have that happen because of the disappointing seasons in Columbus and Ann Arbor. But pride is plenty in this rivalry, and this game still means a ton -- it always does. And for all the Buckeyes ' struggles this season, there are real reasons to like them in The Game. Here are five reasons we believe Scarlet and Gray will be the better colors over Maize and Blue. 1. Jeremiah Smith is the best player on the field This one is simple. Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith is the Heisman frontrunner , the Big Ten's all-time receiving yards leader , and the most talented player either team has. He's caught 86 passes for 1,482 yards and 17 touchdowns this season. He's scored in eight straight games. Michigan has held him in check in two career games -- eight catches for 75 yards. But Smith is playing the best football of his life right now, coming off a 165-yard, two-touchdown game at Nebraska . The Wolverines can double him. They can bracket him. Sooner or later, he's going to make a play that changes the game. 2. He wasn't wrong. Michigan ranks No. 131 in the country in scoring at 18.3 points per game. The Wolverines have flip-flopped between Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback all season. Their leading receiver, J.J. Buchanan, is out for the year with a shoulder injury. Ohio State's defense has had its problems -- 30-plus points in three of the last four games. But Michigan's offense is the worst unit either team will face all season. The Buckeyes should be able to keep the Wolverines under 20 points. That might be enough in this one. 3. The energy in Ohio Stadium on Saturday will be about more than a 7-4 team playing a 6-5 team. It'll be about a rivalry, and a coach, and a season that needs one good day to make a very disappointing season not feel as bad. 4. item.title: Cristian Chivu hails Lautaro Martinez's instant Champions League impact as Inter down Stuttgart
item.description: FC Internazionale Milano v VfB Stuttgart - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Inter coach Cristian Chivu has highlighted the importance of Lautaro Martinez's return to the scoresheet following a crucial Champions League victory over Stuttgart. The Nerazzurri boss was quick to praise his captain's immediate influence after a difficult period for the Italian giants. Lautaro provides the spark Inter moved within a single point of the Champions League top eight on Tuesday night after a professional performance secured a much-needed victory over Stuttgart . It was a near-perfect European night for the Nerazzurri, who paired a much-needed clean sheet with a victory that moves them within a single point. While the entire squad stepped up, it was the sight of Lautaro finding the back of the net almost immediately after stepping onto the pitch that drew the warmest reaction from his manager. "The goal from the Toro? Beauty, quality, it’s all there. But they are top-level players. Lautaro made everyone happy, the bench, the fans, and also defenders and midfielders," Chivu said, as quoted by La Gazzetta dello Sport . Chivu hails Lautaro's timely confidence boost Following a bruising defeat in Bergamo against Atalanta, Chivu’s side responded with a display defined by tactical discipline and clinical finishing. Luka Sucic impressed in a deep-lying role while Francesco Pio Esposito continued his fine form. Chivu was full of praise for Martinez, noting that while the striker's quality was never in question, the goal serves as a massive psychological boost for the entire squad during this busy period of the European campaign. "I thought you would ask me if the fifth striker is missing… At the moment I have three, all good: Lautaro, after the spell in Bergamo, put some minutes in his legs," Chivu remarked. "Mentally for a striker, scoring is a breath of confidence and self-esteem, even if he didn't need it. I am also happy with Pio and Marcus for what they put on the pitch, I hope they stay at these levels but we are aware of the fact that strikers live for collective and personal joys: we must pay great attention regarding their integrity. There are many games and we need them, we hope Bonny returns soon too." Focus shifts back to Serie A Chivu was quick to pivot the focus back to their domestic responsibilities. item.title: 2026 MVBrewers #6: Aaron Ashby
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 27: Aaron Ashby #26 of the Milwaukee Brewers interacts with teammates in the dugout during the eleventh inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game four of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field on October 27, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The votes are in for our No. 6 spot in this year’s MVBrewers rankings, and it’s the pitcher who had far and away the best postseason: Aaron Ashby. Ashby garnered 47 of the 79 total votes (59.5%), with the other 32 votes scattered across Garrett Mitchell (12 votes), Trevor Megill (nine votes), Logan Henderson (eight votes), Abner Uribe (two votes), and Robert Gasser (one write-in vote from @jorgejuliomachado). Ashby, still just 28, debuted with the Brewers all the way back in 2021. After beginning his career as a starter, Ashby missed the entire 2023 season due to arm injuries. He returned in 2024, making 14 appearances (two starts) before becoming a staple of Milwaukee’s bullpen in 2025. After a great 2025 season — he made 43 appearances, spanning 66 2/3 innings with a 2.16 ERA, 2.70 FIP, and 76 strikeouts — he was Pat Murphy’s most-used arm in 2026, making 75 appearances, totaling 89 1/3 innings with a 3.12 ERA, 3.11 FIP, and 116 strikeouts. While he had a few shaky moments in the middle of the season (he had a 6.57 ERA across 24 2/3 innings in June and July) and walked opposing hitters at the highest clip of his career (4.1 BB/9), he was a formidable set-up arm to the back of the Brewers’ bullpen, anchored by Abner Uribe and Trevor Megill. Ashby came up especially clutch late in the year, when Uribe missed some time, leaving Milwaukee without their set-up man. Across 24 appearances in August and September, Ashby totaled 28 2/3 innings, allowing just five earned runs (1.59 ERA) and striking out 33 batters. Then came the postseason. Across nine appearances, Ashby spanned 18 innings. What happened in those 18 innings? No runs allowed (breaking a major league record) on five hits and three walks, striking out 20. item.title: Rookie Watch: This Year’s Calder Trophy Race Could Be One for the Ages
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We’re not even two months into the 2026-27 NHL season, and I already have no idea who I’d pick to win the Calder Trophy. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly have been putting up ridiculous offensive numbers, Cole Hutson is threatening to do something only four defensemen have accomplished in the NHL’s modern era, and Jacob Fowler has been incredible between the pipes. And as good as those four have been, I’m not ready to rule out any of Gavin McKenna, Ivar Stenberg or Viggo Björck, either. I figured the Calder Trophy race would be a pretty good place to start Rookie Watch, a new weekly column where I’ll be keeping tabs on some of the NHL’s most interesting rookies throughout the season. Roman Kantserov and Trevor Connelly Are Making Their Presence Felt Kantserov has scored five goals over his past two games, recording his first career NHL hat trick against the Vancouver Canucks on Sunday before scoring twice against the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday. The 22-year-old Russian forward is now up to 15 goals and 20 points through his first 25 NHL games with the Chicago Blackhawks. According to NHL.com, his 15 goals are the most by any Blackhawks player through the first 25 games of a season since 1943-44. Chicago selected Kantserov 44th overall in the 2023 NHL Draft before watching him develop into one of the most dangerous offensive players in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). There hasn’t been much of an adjustment period for him offensively since making the jump to North America. Connelly, meanwhile, entered Wednesday with nine goals and 19 points through 26 games with the Vegas Golden Knights, including seven points over his previous five games. What’s impressed me about Connelly is his ability to create offense with the puck on his stick, using his skating and creativity to open up space for himself and his teammates. He’s also managed to produce at that rate while averaging less than 15 minutes of ice time per game. I’d love to see what he could do with a little more offensive responsibility in Vegas. Cole Hutson Is Doing Something We Rarely See From Rookie Defensemen Hutson sat atop the NHL’s rookie scoring leaderboard earlier this month, and what I found most impressive was that he was the only defenseman anywhere near the top of it. After scoring his sixth goal of the season against the Philadelphia Flyers on Wednesday, Hutson is up to 16 points through 22 games, putting him on pace for roughly 61 points over an 84-game season. Only four defensemen have led all NHL rookies in scoring since 1943-44. Bobby Orr did it with 41 points in 1966-67, Brian Leetch with 71 in 1988-89, Quinn Hughes with 53 in 2019-20 and, of course, Cole’s older brother Lane Hutson with 66 in 2024-25. As impressive as Kantserov and Connelly have been, Hutson is keeping pace with them while averaging nearly 20 minutes of ice time per game on the blue line. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect One of my biggest criticisms of Scott Arniel since he took over as head coach of the Winnipeg Jets has been his reluctance to change his lines. It often felt like he was sending the same combinations over the boards every night regardless of who the Jets were playing, how certain players were performing or what was happening within the game. It was a criticism I had of Rick Bowness, too, and at times I wondered how much of it was coming from above the coaching staff. When you see some of the same tendencies carry over from one coach to the next, I think it’s fair to question how much of it is an organizational philosophy rather than an individual coaching preference. Whatever the case may be, I’ve really liked what I’ve seen from Arniel lately. The Jets have now won nine of their past 11 games following a 4-2 victory over the Boston Bruins Wednesday, and Arniel deserves some credit for his willingness to try different things throughout the lineup. Morgan Barron scored the game-winning goal for the second consecutive game Wednesday, and how he found himself on the ice with Cole Perfetti and Dawson Mercer is a great example of the growth we’re seeing from Arniel as a head coach. Scott Arniel Is Getting More Out of His Lineup Barron’s game-winning goal against the Utah Mammoth on Monday came courtesy of a beautiful pass from Viggo Björck, but he found himself centering the fourth line between Cole Koepke and Tyrel Bauer at Wednesday’s morning skate. Arniel wasn’t married to the combinations he put together that morning either, though. Perfetti and Mercer spent 6:44 alongside Brayden Yager and another 4:03 alongside Barron, who ended up scoring the game-winning goal after Arniel put him out with the two forwards for an offensive-zone faceoff late in the second period. I don’t necessarily want Barron permanently occupying a top-six center spot, but there’s nothing wrong with putting him there when Arniel sees an opportunity to get something out of that combination. There’s no reason the Jets need to have the exact same third line on the road without last change against Boston as they do at home with last change against Utah, either. Different teams present different challenges, and Winnipeg has enough versatile forwards to give Arniel some options. There’s something to be said for establishing chemistry and giving players an opportunity to get comfortable playing together, but that doesn’t mean you can’t experiment with different combinations throughout a game. The Bounty Bowl As an impressionable 13-year-old boy, the 1989 Bounty Bowl was a seminal moment of my childhood. I think all late-stage Generation X Eagles fans would say the same. After dominating the sport, and the Philadelphia franchise as “America’s Team” for the better part of three decades, the Cowboys had fallen to depths they’d never seen before. And at long last, the Eagles were finally the better team. Dallas was on its way to a 1-15 record, while the Eagles were establishing themselves as a playoff contender. item.title: Parkin to step down as Wrexham assistant
item.description: Steve Parkin won three promotions in five and a half years as Wrexham assistant manager [Getty Images] Steve Parkin will leave his role as Wrexham's assistant manager after Saturday's game with Portsmouth on Saturday, 30 November. The 61-year-old joined Wrexham along with manager Phil Parkinson in 2021 and helped the club win three successive promotions to rise from the National League to the Championship. He says he is stepping away to spend more time with his family. "My time at Wrexham has been truly special," said Parkin. "While the three promotions have been unforgettable achievements, it is the relationships that I will treasure most. "The people of Wrexham have made my family so welcome, and we have made friendships that will last a lifetime." Parkinson encouraged but wants more from Wrexham An England Under-21s international as a player, Parkin's early managerial career included spells with Mansfield, Barnsley and Rochdale before helping Phil Brown win promotion to the Premier League with Hull City. He first joined Parkinson at Bradford City in 2011, reaching a League Cup final. The pair also won promotion to the Championship with Bolton and worked together at Sunderland before moving to Wrexham. "We've managed more than 750 games together, which has included five promotions and many other unforgettable moments," said Parkinson. "Steve has been a consummate professional in every aspect of his work, he's humble and honest, but more importantly he's a top-class person and a great friend. "He's been outstanding for Wrexham AFC over the last five years, and everyone throughout the club appreciate what he has contributed, and I know the supporters will give him a fantastic reception in his final game on Saturday." Under Parkinson and Parkin, Wrexham secured a club highest seventh place in the Championship in 2025-26, having been brought to the Racecourse by owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac shortly after their takeover of the club. "I would like to take this opportunity to thank Rob and Ryan for their incredible support, vision and wisdom in driving the transformation of our football club," added Parkin, who has also been a prominent figure in the Welcome to Wrexham documentary series. "I am incredibly proud of everything we have achieved over the last five and a half years." Acting chief executive Shaun Harvey added: "Steve is a special person, to whom Wrexham owe a big debt of gratitude. "His victory salute made famous in the documentary will be forever linked with our success and is recognition for the significant part he played in it. "Go well Steve and enjoy the time at home, you have more than earned it." Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

item.title: Dolphins' Kyle McCord honors his rescue dog with My Cause My Cleats
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS — Kyle McCord and his fiance, Sophia, adopted Junior from an animal rescue in South Mississippi more than two years ago. "Half pitbull, a quarter labrador and a quarter german shepherd," McCord was saying at his locker prior to his third start as quarterback for the Miami Dolphins . "He's just, he's the man. He smiles when he gets excited, he likes to show his teeth, which is funny." McCord has a passion for dogs, as he and his family have fostered and adopted at least four dogs. "My dog now is my best friend and just kind of seeing what some of those animals have to go through is tough," McCord said. McCord will wear cleats on Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium with the logo and name of "Misfits & Underdogs" the animal rescue in Mississippi that is "fighting for the discarded, the overlooked, and the underdogs." "A cause that’s near and dear to my heart," said McCord, who wants to raise awareness for pet adoption by participating in the NFL's "My Cause My Cleats" initiative. Like anyone who has had a dog knows, McCord says the emotional connection he has with Junior is invaluable. "Life is obviously, in the NFL, crazy," McCord said. "It's like all the twists and turns, and one day you feel like you're in a great position, and the next day you're like, 'Oh, what's happening?' But being able to come home and having a pet that just doesn't care, just wants to make you happy, and be around you and is just always in a good mood, I feel like it has definitely brought a real sense of joy to my life." McCord adopted his dog when he lived in Philadelphia. "Literally, all we had to pay for was the transport and a few of the shots for him to get here," McCord said. "And he's been great. He's had no problems. None of the dogs have had any problems health wise. So, yeah, I've got nothing but good things to say about Misfits and Underdogs." McCord was dealt from the Packers to the Dolphins on Aug. 30, just two weeks before Miami's season opened. "Finding a place that accepts dogs," McCord said of a residence search, "that was definitely priority number one." item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
